chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Discipline the orphan with the same discipline you use for your own child, and strike him with the same strikes you use for your own child.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: How should an orphan be disciplined according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter governing the rights of divorced women’s children, this narration from Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of equity in upbringing, ensuring orphans receive the same disciplinary standards and affection as biological offspring. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the *kafala* (guardianship) responsibilities, emphasizing that the guardian’s role extends beyond mere provision to include moral and educational nurturing identical to that of a father.
